mainTopic: Who is exempt from סוכה (מצוה-doers, travelers, guards, the sick and suffering), and the rules of casual eating and sleeping (סוכה 26a)
overview: This עמוד continues the list of people who are exempt from סוכה. It starts with רבי שילא's view that only the חתן is exempt, and with רבי חנניא בן עקביא's ruling that scribes and sellers of holy items are exempt from other מצוות, based on העוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה. Ordinary travelers and city guards are exempt only during the hours they travel or guard, but someone traveling for a מצוה is exempt even while resting. Guards of gardens and orchards are always exempt, and אביי and רבא give different reasons why. Next, the גמרא teaches that even a mildly sick person and his attendants are exempt. Then רבא's rule that a מצטער is exempt, though his attendants are not, is defended against the משנה. The גמרא then defines אכילת עראי and explains why even a short nap outside the סוכה is forbidden. That leads to a discussion of sleeping in תפילין, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבי שילא: only the חתן is exempt, not his wedding party
steps.stepSummary: רבי שילא disagrees with the preceding ברייתא. He says only the חתן is exempt, while the שושבינין and the rest of the wedding party remain obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי שילא they said: The חתן is exempt, but the groomsmen and all the members of the wedding party are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא it was quoting about a חתן and his friends by adding a second opinion, from רבי שילא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the ברייתא (on the previous עמוד) treated the חתן and his whole wedding party the same way. רבי שילא splits them. Only the חתן himself is preoccupied enough to be exempt (from קריאת שמע, per the context), while the friends who celebrate with him are still obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: Groomsmen, the close friends who escort and celebrate with the groom

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the closing, dissenting opinion of a ברייתא that began on the previous עמוד, so 'exempt' refers back to the מצוות discussed there.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Sheila they said:
A groom is exempt,
phrases.notes: His mind is taken up with his wedding, which is itself a מצוה.

phrases.english: but the groomsmen and all the members of the wedding party are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד about the חתן and his party, offering a dissenting view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the חתן is exempt. The שושבינין and בני החופה are obligated.

steps.title: Scribes and sellers of holy items are exempt from other מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בן עקביא rules that people writing or selling ספרי תורה, תפילין, and מזוזות, along with anyone doing 'heavenly work', are exempt from קריאת שמע, תפלה, תפילין, and all other מצוות while they work.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי חנניא בן עקביא said: Scribes of ספרי תורה, תפילין, and מזוזות are exempt. So are the merchants who sell these items, the merchants who buy from those merchants, and everyone involved in heavenly work, which includes sellers of תכלת. They are exempt from קריאת שמע, from תפלה, from תפילין, and from all the מצוות mentioned in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives a broad list of people who are exempt from מצוות because they are busy with holy work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list moves outward from the scribe himself, to the merchants, to the merchants' merchants, and then to anyone doing מלאכת שמים. The גמרא adds the word לאתויי to say that this last phrase is meant to include sellers of תכלת. The exemption is very wide: it covers every מצוה in the תורה, not just סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Their merchants, who sell the holy items
Heavenly work, labor done for a holy purpose
To include (the גמרא's note on what a phrase adds)
The sky-blue dye used for ציצית

steps.confusionAlert: Even the merchants are exempt, not just the scribes. Selling these items gets them into the hands of people who need them, and that counts as being busy with a מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Ḥananya ben Akavya said:
Scribes of Torah scrolls, tefillin, and mezuzot,
they themselves, their merchants, and the merchants of their merchants,
and all who are engaged in the labor of Heaven,
which comes to include sellers of sky-blue dye,
phrases.notes: These words are the גמרא explaining what the line comes to include.

phrases.english: are exempt from reciting Shema and from prayer
and from tefillin
and from all מצוות mentioned in the Torah,

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the discussion from the חתן to anyone busy with holy work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those engaged in writing or selling holy items, or in any מלאכת שמים, are exempt from all other מצוות while engaged.

steps.title: The source principle: one busy with a מצוה is exempt from another
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that its ruling follows רבי יוסי הגלילי's general rule: העוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is to fulfill the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי, for רבי יוסי הגלילי used to say: One who is engaged in a מצוה is exempt from another מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the reason behind the exemption it just listed. It points to a famous general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of scribes and merchants is an application of a larger principle. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that being busy with one מצוה frees a person from a second one that comes up at the same time. This rule also explains the חתן and the travelers who appear next.

keyTerms.meaning: To fulfill or uphold the words of
One who is engaged in a מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה: someone actively busy with one מצוה is exempt from another. This is the engine behind much of this סוגיא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle has major practical weight across ש״ס and in הלכה. It defines when a person doing one מצוה may set aside another.

phrases.english: to fulfill the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
for Rabbi Yosei HaGelili would say:
One who is engaged in a מצוה is exempt from a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the underlying reason for the ruling in step 2.

steps.title: Travelers are exempt from סוכה only during their travel time
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that ordinary travelers are exempt from סוכה only during the hours they travel: by day, by night, or both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: People traveling during the day are exempt from סוכה during the day and obligated at night. People traveling at night are exempt from סוכה at night and obligated during the day. People traveling both day and night are exempt from סוכה both day and night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about travelers and lays out three cases based on when they travel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular traveler is not doing a מצוה. His exemption comes from the fact that the תורה does not require a person to stop living his normal life. You live in a סוכה the way you live in your home, and people do travel away from home. So the exemption lasts only while he is actually on the road. When he stops, he is obligated again.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Travelers by day

phrases.aramaic: פְּטוּרִין מִן הַסּוּכָּה בַּיּוֹם, וְחַיָּיבִין בַּלַּיְלָה.
phrases.english: are exempt from sukkah by day and obligated at night.
Travelers by night

phrases.aramaic: פְּטוּרִין מִן הַסּוּכָּה בַּלַּיְלָה וְחַיָּיבִין בַּיּוֹם.
phrases.english: are exempt from sukkah at night and obligated by day.
Travelers by day and by night
are exempt from sukkah
both by day and by night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a different kind of exemption from סוכה: travel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ordinary traveler is exempt from סוכה only during the time he is traveling.

steps.title: Travelers for a מצוה are exempt day and night
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that people traveling for a מצוה are exempt from סוכה at all times, even during hours they are not actually traveling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those who travel for a מצוה are exempt both during the day and at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a fourth case, travel for a מצוה, which gets a wider exemption than ordinary travel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary traveler is exempt only while moving. Someone traveling for a מצוה is exempt even when he rests, because the whole trip counts as being busy with a מצוה. This applies רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule from step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter of מצוה; a מצוה purpose

steps.confusionAlert: These people are exempt day and night even if they travel only by day. The reason for the trip, not the travel hours, determines their exemption.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the distinction between a regular traveler and a שליח מצוה, which the story that follows illustrates.

phrases.english: Those who travel for a matter of מצוה
are exempt both by day and by night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the ordinary travelers of step 4 and gives a broader exemption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One traveling for a מצוה is exempt from סוכה at all times.

steps.title: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא sleep by the river
steps.stepSummary: A story shows the rule in action. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא, on their way to the ריש גלותא's festival lecture, slept on the bank of the Sura River and not in a סוכה, because they were שלוחי מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what happened with רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא. When they would go to the house of the ריש גלותא on the שבת of the festival, they slept on the riverbank of Sura. They said: We are on a מצוה mission, and we are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life case of אמוראים relying on the rule that people traveling for a מצוה are exempt from סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going to hear the ריש גלותא's festival lecture counted as a מצוה trip. So even while they were resting and not traveling, they did not need a סוכה. Their own words, 'we are שלוחי מצוה', state the reason directly.

keyTerms.meaning: The Shabbat of the festival, when a public festival lecture was given
The Exilarch, leader of the Babylonian Jewish community
Messengers or travelers on a מצוה mission

steps.whatToRemember: An ordinary traveler is exempt only while traveling. A שליח מצוה is exempt the whole time, as רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא showed.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: As in this case of Rav Ḥisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna:
when they would go in on the Shabbat of the Festival
to the house of the Exilarch,
they would sleep on the riverbank of Sura,
phrases.notes: They slept outside, not in a סוכה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: אֲנַן שְׁלוּחֵי מִצְוָה אֲנַן וּפְטוּרִין.
phrases.english: They said: We are on a מצוה mission, and we are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the rule of step 5 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that those traveling for a מצוה are exempt from סוכה even while resting.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא on their way to the ריש גלותא.

steps.title: City guards are exempt from סוכה during their guarding hours
steps.stepSummary: A parallel ברייתא applies the same day/night pattern to שומרי העיר: they are exempt only during the hours they guard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Guards of the city by day are exempt from סוכה by day and obligated at night. Guards of the city at night are exempt from סוכה at night and obligated by day. Guards of the city both day and night are exempt from סוכה both day and night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא, about city guards, built exactly like the travelers ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A guard cannot leave his post to sit in a סוכה, so he is exempt while on duty. When his shift ends, the obligation returns. This matches the ordinary traveler, not the שליח מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Guardians or watchmen of the city

steps.whatToRemember: For ordinary travelers and city guards, the exemption follows the hours of activity. Only someone traveling for a מצוה is exempt even during the hours he is not traveling.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Guardians of the city by day

phrases.aramaic: פְּטוּרִין מִן הַסּוּכָּה בַּיּוֹם, וְחַיָּיבִין בַּלַּיְלָה.
phrases.english: are exempt from sukkah by day and obligated at night.
Guardians of the city at night

phrases.aramaic: פְּטוּרִין מִן הַסּוּכָּה בַּלַּיְלָה, וְחַיָּיבִין בַּיּוֹם.
phrases.english: are exempt from sukkah at night and obligated by day.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמְרֵי הָעִיר בֵּין בַּיּוֹם וּבֵין בַּלַּיְלָה —
phrases.english: Guardians of the city both by day and by night

phrases.aramaic: פְּטוּרִים מִן הַסּוּכָּה בֵּין בַּיּוֹם וּבֵין בַּלַּיְלָה.
phrases.english: are exempt from sukkah both by day and by night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא that follows the same structure as the travelers ברייתא in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: City guards are exempt from סוכה only during the hours they guard.

steps.title: Garden and orchard guards are exempt day and night
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: guards of gardens and orchards are exempt from סוכה at all times, by day and by night.
steps.simpleTranslation: People who guard gardens and orchards are exempt from סוכה both during the day and at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second kind of guard. Unlike city guards, garden guards are fully exempt, day and night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, שומרי העיר were exempt only during the hours they actually guard. Here שומרי גנות ופרדסים get a complete exemption. This contrast is what makes the גמרא ask its next question.

phrases.english: Guards of gardens and orchards
are exempt both by day and by night.
phrases.notes: Compare city guards (Step 7), who were exempt only during their guarding hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹמְרֵי גַנּוֹת וּפַרְדֵּסִים פְּטוּרִין בֵּין בַּיּוֹם וּבֵין בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא about guards, giving a contrasting case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Garden and orchard guards are exempt from סוכה at all times.

steps.title: Why not build a סוכה right in the garden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the exemption: the guards could simply build a סוכה in the garden and sit in it while guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them build a סוכה there in the garden and sit in it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ruling it just heard. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Guarding happens in one place, so it seems possible to guard and keep the מצוה at the same time. If so, why give a full exemption?

phrases.english: But let them make a sukkah there and sit in it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the full exemption given in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The full exemption of garden guards.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The guards could fulfill סוכה on site, so an exemption seems unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: a סוכה must be like your home
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the פסוק "תשבו" means living in the סוכה the way you live at home. A guard cannot move his whole household out to the orchard.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: "You shall dwell" means dwelling the way you normally live.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer. A סוכה in the orchard would not be a real home-like dwelling for the guard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule תשבו כעין תדורו requires the סוכה to work like your regular home. Setting up a full home in a distant orchard is too much to demand, so the obligation never applies to this guard.

keyTerms.meaning: you shall dwell (the verse about living in the סוכה)

steps.whyThisMatters: תשבו כעין תדורו is a basic principle of סוכה law that comes up in many places.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
"You shall dwell" means like the way you live.
phrases.notes: The guard cannot move his home life into the orchard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines what the מצוה requires (a home-like dwelling).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any סוכה built on site should work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The obligation is to dwell as at home, which is impossible for the guard in the orchard.

steps.title: רבא: a guard sitting still invites thieves
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently. If the guard sits in a סוכה, thieves will know where he is and break in somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: An opening calls to the thief.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second, different answer to the same question. His reason is practical, based on how guarding actually works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A guard must move around. Fixing him in one סוכה leaves the rest of the garden open, and the thieves will take advantage of it.

phrases.english: Rava said: A breach calls to the thief.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 9's challenge, parallel to אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical: sitting in a סוכה would undermine the guarding.
steps.terutzMaskana: The guard must be free to move, so he is exempt.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what case אביי and רבא would actually rule differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a case where the two reasons lead to different results. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons exempt the ordinary garden guard. The גמרא wants a case that tells them apart.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers in Steps 10–11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where אביי and רבא would rule differently.

steps.title: The difference: guarding a pile of fruit
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a guard watching a single pile of fruit. He can watch it from inside a סוכה, so רבא would obligate him, while אביי would still exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference when he is guarding a pile of fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the case where the two reasons split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single pile can be watched from one spot, so רבא's worry about thieves does not apply and the guard must sit in a סוכה. For אביי, the orchard still is not his home, so he stays exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: exempt because a סוכה must be like home. רבא: exempt because the guard must move around. They differ about a guard watching one pile of fruit.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he is guarding a pile of fruit.
phrases.notes: One spot can be watched from a סוכה: רבא obligates, אביי exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּקָא מְנַטַּר כַּרְיָא דְפֵירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ about a guard watching a pile of fruit.

steps.title: Even a mildly sick person is exempt
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה's case of the sick and their attendants, a ברייתא rules that the exemption covers even someone not in danger, even someone with sore eyes or a headache.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said "the sick and their attendants." The Rabbis taught: the sick person they meant is not only someone in danger, but even someone who is not in danger, even someone whose eyes hurt or whose head hurts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the משנה's next case and brings a ברייתא that explains how broad it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think only a seriously ill person is exempt. The ברייתא extends the exemption to minor illness, as small as eye pain or a headache.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase לא חולה שיש בו סכנה does not mean a dangerously ill person is NOT exempt. It means not ONLY him. Even a mildly ill person is exempt.

phrases.english: The sick and their attendants.
The Rabbis taught:
The sick person they spoke of
is not only a sick person who is in danger,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ חוֹלֶה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ סַכָּנָה.
phrases.english: but even a sick person who is not in danger.
Even one whose eyes hurt,
and even one whose head hurts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, the sick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any sick person, even one with minor pain, is exempt from סוכה.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's eye pain in Caesarea
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל tells how רבי יוסי ברבי allowed him and his attendant to sleep outside the סוכה because his eyes hurt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: Once my eyes hurt in Caesarea, and רבי יוסי ברבי allowed me and my attendant to sleep outside the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: A real-life story backs up the ברייתא's rule about minor illness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eye pain is a minor, non-dangerous illness, and it still earned an exemption. The attendant was exempt too, which matches the משנה's "and their attendants."

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
Once my eyes hurt in Caesarea,
and the esteemed Rabbi Yosei permitted
me and my attendant to sleep outside the sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל פַּעַם אַחַת חַשְׁתִּי בְּעֵינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 14 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: Minor illness (eye pain) exempts both the patient and his attendant.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A personal story told by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: רב allows sleeping under a canopy because of flies
steps.stepSummary: רב allowed רב אחא ברדלא to sleep under a canopy inside the סוכה because of biting flies, even though this is not proper סוכה sleeping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב permitted רב אחא ברדלא to sleep under a canopy in the סוכה because of the flies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story where discomfort, not illness, led to a leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tall canopy forms its own tent, so sleeping under it is like sleeping outside the סוכה. רב still allowed it, because the flies made the סוכה uncomfortable.

phrases.english: Rav permitted Rav Acha Bardela
to sleep under a canopy in the sukkah
phrases.notes: A tall canopy is its own tent, cutting him off from the סוכה's covering.

phrases.english: because of the flies.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׁרָא לְרַב אַחָא בַּרְדְּלָא לְמִגְנֵא בְּכִילְּתָא בַּסּוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practical leniency, here based on discomfort.
steps.raayaObject: Discomfort can justify leaving proper סוכה sleeping.

steps.title: רבא allows sleeping outside because of a bad smell
steps.stepSummary: רבא allowed רבי אחא בר אדא to sleep outside the סוכה because of the foul smell of the clay floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא permitted רבי אחא בר אדא to sleep outside the סוכה because of the bad smell of the clay.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story shows discomfort letting someone sleep outside the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the problem is a bad smell, not illness. Together with רב's case, it shows that real discomfort can release a person from sleeping in the סוכה.
steps.whatToRemember: Illness, even minor, exempts a person from סוכה. Real discomfort (flies, a bad smell) can also allow sleeping outside it.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא שְׁרָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא
phrases.english: Rava permitted Rabbi Acha bar Adda
to sleep outside the sukkah
because of the bad smell of the clay.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא שְׁרָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא לְמִגְנֵא בַּר מִמְּטַלַּלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel case to Step 16, with a different kind of discomfort.
steps.raayaObject: A bad smell is enough discomfort to sleep outside the סוכה.

steps.title: רבא's ruling follows his own rule about a person who is suffering
steps.stepSummary: The story of רבא matches his known rule that a מצטער is פטור from סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא follows his own reasoning, because רבא said: someone who is suffering is exempt from the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא let רבי אחא בר אדא sleep outside the סוכה (step 17). It is because רבא holds a general rule: a person who suffers in the סוכה is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story was not a one-time leniency. It follows a fixed principle of רבא: a מצטער, someone who is uncomfortable but not sick, is פטור. This sets up the next question, since the משנה only mentions the sick.

keyTerms.meaning: following his own reasoning (consistent with his known view)
one who is suffering or uncomfortable

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of מצטער פטור מן הסוכה is a central and practical halacha of סוכה.

phrases.english: Rava follows his own reasoning,
for Rava said:
One who suffers is exempt from the sukka.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבא's story in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצטער is פטור from סוכה.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה exempts only the sick
steps.stepSummary: The משנה exempts חולין, which implies that a mere מצטער is not exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: the sick and their attendants are exempt from the סוכה. This implies that a sick person is exempt, but someone who is only suffering is not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's rule using the משנה. If the משנה names only the sick, that seems to show that ordinary discomfort does not exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is a precise reading of the משנה. Since it says חולין and not מצטערין, the גמרא reasons that only the sick are exempt. That would contradict רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: but have we not learned (in the משנה)
yes... no (this case, but not that one)

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the mishna:
The sick and their caretakers are exempt from the sukka.
A sick person, yes; one who suffers, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's rule from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a מצטער is פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names only חולין, which implies a מצטער is not exempt.

steps.title: Answer: the difference is whether the attendants are exempt
steps.stepSummary: Both the sick and the suffering are exempt, but only a sick person's attendants are also exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: a sick person and his attendants are exempt. Someone who is only suffering is exempt himself, but his attendants are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה mentions the sick because of the attendants. Only for a sick person are the attendants exempt too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's point is not that only the sick are exempt. Its point is that their attendants are exempt as well. A מצטער still exempts himself, but the people helping him must stay in the סוכה.
steps.whatToRemember: A חולה and his attendants are פטור. A מצטער is פטור himself, but his attendants are not.

phrases.english: They say:
A sick person: he and his caretakers are exempt;
one who suffers: he is exempt, his caretakers are not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the משנה's purpose: it is about the attendants' exemption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's mention of חולין implies a מצטער is obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are exempt. The משנה names חולין to teach that their attendants are exempt too.

steps.title: How much food counts as a casual meal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that permits אכילת עראי outside the סוכה and asks how much that is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: one may eat a casual meal outside the סוכה. How much is a casual meal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It asks what amount of food is still called a casual snack rather than a real meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows casual eating outside the סוכה, but it gives no amount. The גמרא needs to define the boundary between עראי (casual) and קבע (a fixed meal).

keyTerms.meaning: casual or temporary eating, a snack

phrases.english: One may eat a casual meal outside the sukka.
And how much is a casual meal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of food that still counts as אכילת עראי.

steps.title: רב יוסף: two or three egg-sizes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says a casual meal is two or three ביצים of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: two or three egg-sizes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a measurement. Eating up to two or three egg-volumes of bread is still casual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He defines עראי by a fixed amount of food, using the ביצה as the unit of measure.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Two or three egg-bulks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two or three ביצים of bread.

steps.title: אביי: that amount is often a full meal
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that many people are satisfied with that much, so it is really a סעודת קבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: but often a person is satisfied with that much, so it counts as a fixed meal!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's measurement. For many people, two or three eggs' worth of bread is a full meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an amount can fully satisfy a person, it cannot be called a snack. So רב יוסף's measure is too large.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But often
a person is satisfied with this,
and it is a formal meal!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא זִימְנִין סַגִּיאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's measure of two or three ביצים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That amount often fully satisfies a person, so it is a סעודת קבע, not עראי.

steps.title: אביי: as much as a student eats before a lecture
steps.stepSummary: אביי defines עראי as the quick bite a yeshiva student takes before going in to the lecture.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: like the amount a student of the ישיבה tastes before he goes in to the lecture.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רב יוסף, אביי gives his own definition. A casual meal is the small bite a student grabs before going in to the שיעור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי defines עראי by the kind of eating, not by a fixed number. It is a quick bite taken on the way to something else, and it does not satisfy the person.

keyTerms.meaning: the public lecture or study gathering

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, אכילת עראי is a small bite taken before going off to learn, not an amount that fills you.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
like what a student of the academy tastes
and then enters for the lecture.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The small amount a student eats before entering the lecture.

steps.title: ברייתא: casual eating is allowed outside the סוכה, but casual sleep is not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא permits a snack outside the סוכה but forbids even a nap.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: one may eat a casual meal outside the סוכה, but one may not sleep even a casual nap outside the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that treats eating and sleeping differently. A snack is allowed outside, but even a short nap is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both eating and sleeping are normally obligations in the סוכה. So it is surprising that the casual version of eating is permitted while the casual version of sleeping is forbidden. This sets up the next question.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may eat a casual meal outside the sukka,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין יְשֵׁנִים שֵׁינַת עֲרַאי חוּץ לַסּוּכָּה.
phrases.english: but one may not take a brief nap outside the sukka.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that contrasts eating with sleeping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אכילת עראי is permitted outside the סוכה, but שינת עראי is forbidden.

steps.title: Why is a nap different from a snack?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ברייתא's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why sleeping is stricter than eating. This short question sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both are obligations in the סוכה, the casual form of each should be treated the same. The גמרא wants to know what makes sleep different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why שינת עראי is forbidden outside the סוכה while אכילת עראי is allowed.

steps.title: רב אשי: a decree, in case he falls into deep sleep
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that a short nap is forbidden as a גזירה, because it might turn into a long sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: it is a decree, in case he falls into a deep sleep.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that the רבנן forbade even a nap. A person cannot control how long he sleeps, so a nap could easily become a full sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A snack has a clear end that the person controls. Sleep does not. So the רבנן made a protective decree against even casual sleep.

keyTerms.meaning: lest he fall into a deep sleep

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
A decree, lest he fall into deep sleep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה, because a nap may become a deep, long sleep.

steps.title: Challenge from napping while wearing tefillin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא permits a brief nap in תפילין. Why are we not worried there that he will fall into deep sleep?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: but what about what was taught, that a person may take a short nap while wearing תפילין, but not a full sleep? Let us worry there too that he will fall into deep sleep!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב אשי's reason. With תפילין, a short nap is allowed and only a full sleep is forbidden, so the same worry should apply there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry about falling into deep sleep is real, it should also forbid napping in תפילין. Since it does not, the reason given for the סוכה law seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: that which was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא:
phrases.english: Abaye said to him: But that which was taught:
A person may take a brief nap in phylacteries,
but not substantial sleep;
let us be concerned lest he fall into deep sleep!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's reason in step 27.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same worry should forbid napping in תפילין, yet that is permitted.

steps.title: Answer: with tefillin he asks others to wake him
steps.stepSummary: For תפילין, the case is one where he puts others in charge of waking him, so there is no worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בריה דרב עילאי said: it is a case where he hands responsibility for his sleep to others.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that the תפילין ruling speaks about someone who asks others to wake him. Since they will wake him, he will not fall into a long sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about deep sleep is removed when other people are watching over him. So the תפילין case does not contradict רב אשי's גזירה for סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: hands over his sleep to others (asks them to wake him)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עִילַּאי:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef, son of Rav Illai, said:
Where he assigns his sleep to others.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עִילַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the תפילין case to a special situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תפילין ruling shows there is no worry of שמא ירדם.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the תפילין case others will wake him, so the worry does not apply. The סוכה גזירה stands.

steps.title: The one who wakes you needs someone to wake him
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא challenges the previous answer. The person put in charge of waking the sleeper might fall asleep too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא objected: Your guarantor needs a guarantor!
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא attacks the answer from Step 29. That answer said a nap in תפילין is fine because others are put in charge of waking the sleeper. He points out that the people in charge might fall asleep themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 29 relied on outside people as a safety net. רב משרשיא says this safety net is not reliable, because then we would need someone to watch the watcher, and so on forever. So the worry about falling into a deep sleep comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor, someone who takes responsibility

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya strongly objected:
Your guarantor needs a guarantor!
phrases.notes: The one who is supposed to wake you could also fall asleep

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that in the תפילין case he appoints others to wake him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The people appointed to wake him can fall asleep too, so they give no real guarantee

steps.title: He sleeps with his head between his knees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a new answer. The תפילין case is one where the person sleeps sitting with his head between his knees, a position where deep sleep is unlikely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: We are dealing with someone who rests his head between his knees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'others will wake him' answer and gives a new one. In the תפילין case, the person sleeps in an uncomfortable position, so he will not slip into a deep sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא means 'rather': the previous answer is thrown out. Instead of relying on other people, the protection now comes from how the person sleeps. Resting your head on your knees does not allow a long, deep sleep, so the worry from Step 28 goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the previous answer and gives a new one)
We are dealing with (a specific case)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: Rather, Rabba bar bar Chana said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
with one who places his head between his knees
phrases.notes: A sitting position that does not allow deep sleep

phrases.english: we are dealing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that Step 30 knocked down
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a specific sleeping position
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A brief nap in תפילין should also be forbidden, because it could become a deep sleep
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא about תפילין deals with someone whose head is between his knees, so deep sleep is not a worry

steps.title: רבא: sleep has no 'short' category
steps.stepSummary: רבא takes a completely different approach. There is no worry about falling into deep sleep in either case. Outside the סוכה, any sleep at all counts as real, settled sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There is no 'fixed' measure for sleep.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the whole question in a different way. He says the reason for the סוכה rule is not a גזירה at all. Any amount of sleep counts as real sleep, so even a nap is forbidden outside the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי (Step 27) said a nap outside the סוכה is forbidden only as a protective fence. רבא says a nap is itself 'real' sleep, so it is forbidden outside the סוכה on its own terms. In that case the תפילין ברייתא causes no contradiction, because we are not worried about deep sleep there either.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed or settled, as opposed to temporary

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not mean that sleep is never long. He means there is no amount of sleep too short to count. Even a short nap is considered real sleep, so it needs a סוכה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
There is no fixed measure for sleep.
phrases.notes: Even a short sleep counts as real sleep

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation that avoids the whole question from Step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the reason behind the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A nap outside the סוכה is forbidden only as a protective גזירה
steps.terutzMaskana: Any sleep counts as real sleep, so the סוכה rule has nothing to do with worrying about deep sleep, and תפילין is no contradiction
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the basis of the סוכה rule from a protective fence into a basic definition of what sleep is.

steps.title: Three ברייתות disagree about sleeping in תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes three ברייתות. One allows only a brief nap in תפילין, one allows any sleep, and one allows no sleep at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: A person may take a brief nap in תפילין but not a settled sleep. Another teaches: both settled sleep and a brief nap are allowed. And another teaches: neither settled sleep nor a brief nap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows three sources that seem to contradict each other about sleeping with תפילין. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three ברייתות cover every possibility: a nap only, everything, and nothing. They cannot all be true about the same situation. So the גמרא must explain how each one fits.

phrases.english: One (baraita) teaches:
A person may sleep in tefillin a brief sleep
but not a settled sleep,

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: בֵּין קֶבַע בֵּין עֲרַאי.
phrases.english: And another teaches: both settled and brief.
phrases.notes: Every kind of sleep is allowed

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: לֹא קֶבַע וְלֹא עֲרַאי.
phrases.english: And another teaches: neither settled nor brief.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a related topic: contradictions among sources about sleeping in תפילין
steps.kashyaTarget: The three ברייתות about sleeping in תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three sources give opposite rulings, so they seem to contradict each other

steps.title: Each ברייתא describes a different situation
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. If he holds the תפילין in his hand, no sleep is allowed. If they are on his head, only a nap is allowed. If he spreads a cloth over them, any sleep is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: This one is where he holds them in his hand. This one is where they are on his head. This one is where he spreads a cloth over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by matching each ברייתא to a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he holds the תפילין in his hand, even a short nap is forbidden, because he might drop them. If they are on his head, a brief nap is fine, but a deep sleep is forbidden because of the worry that he might pass wind or have a seminal emission. If he takes them off and covers them with a cloth, he may sleep as long as he wants.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: Holding תפילין in the hand: no sleep at all. Wearing them on the head: only a brief nap. Covered with a cloth: any sleep.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is where he holds them in his hand.
phrases.notes: Matches the ruling of no sleep at all, because he might drop them

phrases.english: This one is where they rest on his head.
phrases.notes: Matches the ruling of a brief nap only

phrases.english: This one is where he spreads a cloth over them.
phrases.notes: Matches the ruling that any sleep is allowed

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּנָקֵיט לְהוּ בִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 33
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each source refers to a different situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three ברייתות directly contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא refers to a different way the תפילין are positioned

steps.title: How long is a brief nap?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a שינת עראי lasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is a brief nap?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an exact measure of a 'brief nap', since the rules depend on it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several rules now depend on telling a nap apart from real sleep. Without a measure, nobody would know when a nap turns into forbidden sleep. So the גמרא needs a definition.

phrases.english: And how much is a brief sleep?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a term used in the ברייתות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length of time that counts as שינת עראי

steps.title: The time it takes to walk 100 cubits
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל teaches that a brief nap lasts about as long as it takes to walk 100 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר יחזקאל taught: The time it takes to walk one hundred אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a measure: a brief nap is about as long as a walk of 100 אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measure is given in walking time, not in minutes. Any sleep longer than that is no longer a 'brief nap'.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, a measure of length of about an arm's length

phrases.english: Rami bar Yechezkel taught:
The time of walking one hundred cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 35
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A brief nap is the time it takes to walk 100 אמות

steps.title: A supporting ברייתא about seminal emission during sleep
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support: someone who sleeps in תפילין and has a seminal emission grabs the strap to remove them. The ברייתא continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: One who sleeps in תפילין and has a seminal emission holds onto the strap...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that supports what was said before. The quote continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תניא נמי הכי comes right after רמי בר יחזקאל's measure, so it supports the teaching just given. Exactly how this ברייתא proves the point becomes clear only when it is completed on the next עמוד. The part quoted here gives a practical instruction: someone who has a seminal emission while sleeping in תפילין takes hold of the strap to remove them.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)

phrases.notes: He removes them this way. The ברייתא continues on the next עמוד.
